messages.subject: gmultmix() Results & Plotting Covariates
parts:
Hi all, 

I am trying to model abundance for a couple of species using gmultmix() and time of detection data. My models have converged, however, when I try to graph the relationship between my significant predictor variables and abundance, it doesn't seem correct. 

Here is my fitted unmarkedFrameGMM: 
umf.SESP21<- unmarkedFrameGMM(y=SESP.Hmat21,  siteCovs = covs21[,c("EdgeDist", "Dev1km", "Est200", "DS_Percentage", "SP_Percentage")], obsCovs=list(interval=cbind(intervalMat21, intervalMat21, intervalMat21)),yearlySiteCovs=list(date=daymat21, wind=windmat21, observer=nobsmat21),obsToY=o2yGMM, piFun="crPiFun", numPrimary=nVisits)

Here is my best model and summary: 
sallnb21 <- gmultmix(~scale(EdgeDist)+scale(Dev1km)+scale(Est200)+scale(DS_Percentage)+scale(SP_Percentage), ~scale(date), ~scale(date)+scale(wind)+observer, data = umf.SESP21, mixture = "NB", engine = "R")

summary(sallnb21)
Call:
gmultmix(lambdaformula = ~scale(EdgeDist) + scale(Dev1km) + scale(Est200) +
    DS_Percentage + SP_Percentage, phiformula = ~scale(date),
    pformula = ~scale(date) + scale(wind) + observer, data = umf.SESP21,
    mixture = "NB", engine = "R")

Abundance (log-scale):
                Estimate      SE      z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)      0.29812 0.35359  0.843 3.99e-01
scale(EdgeDist)  0.23628 0.13595  1.738 8.22e-02
scale(Dev1km)   -1.16896 0.30997 -3.771 1.62e-04
scale(Est200)    0.81412 0.20467  3.978 6.96e-05
DS_Percentage    0.00543 0.00498  1.091 2.75e-01
SP_Percentage    0.02104 0.00812  2.593 9.52e-03

Availability (logit-scale):
            Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)  -1.8568 0.234 -7.94 2.10e-15
scale(date)   0.0989 0.049  2.02 4.36e-02

Detection (logit-scale):
            Estimate     SE     z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)    0.666 0.0439 15.15 7.63e-52
scale(date)   -0.170 0.0485 -3.50 4.73e-04
scale(wind)    0.117 0.0370  3.16 1.60e-03
observer      -0.536 0.0599 -8.95 3.60e-19

Dispersion (log-scale):
 Estimate    SE    z  P(>|z|)
    -1.39 0.169 -8.2 2.32e-16

AIC: 3678.43
Number of sites: 262
optim convergence code: 0
optim iterations: 84
Bootstrap iterations: 0

Here is the result for when I try to plot the positive significant relationship between SP_Percentage (which is a discrete variable from 0-100 %) and abundance with the code below: 


sp.o <- seq(0,100, length.out=100)
sp.mean <- mean(covs21[,c("SP_Percentage")])
sp.sd <- sd(covs21[,c("SP_Percentage")])
sp <- (sp.o - sp.mean)/sp.sd

spalplot <- data.frame(SP_Percentage=sp, DevDist=0, Dev1km=0, Est200=0, DS_Percentage=0, EdgeDist=0, date=0, wind=0, observer=0)
best.pred <- predict(sallnb21, type="lambda", newdata=spalplot, appendData=TRUE)

plot(Predicted ~ SP_Percentage, best.pred, type="l", ylim=c(0, 2), xlim=c(0,1),
       ylab="Seaside Sparrows / plot", xlab="Percent SPAL")
lines(lower ~ SP_Percentage, best.pred, col=gray(0.7))
lines(upper ~ SP_Percentage, best.pred, col=gray(0.7))

I'm having trouble understanding how this prediction plot is not showing a positive relationship. Maybe it is a lack of fundamental knowledge or an issue with how I'm telling R to treat my covariates. 

Any help/advice/suggestions are very much appreciated. 

Best, 
Rachel

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: gmultmix() Results & Plotting Covariates
parts:
Hi Rachel,

If you are scaling your covariates via the formula interface as you are, you should not then scale the covariates again before supplying them to predict - keep them on the original scales. If you have scale in the formulas predict will handle the scaling automatically. At the moment your covariates are being scaled twice, which may be contributing to your plotting issues.

Ken
